models.is: A durable record (Environment in control state) with a name, desired state (running/stopped), configuration, policy, and optionally an owner, a ComputerSpec, and EnvironmentContents.
models.collision: Two kinds share the name: an environment with a computer, and a "node environment" whose bundle projects run on the daemon host. `applications` is a reserved node environment for `compute deploy <dir>`.

models.is: The machine behind an environment with a ComputerSpec: a Computer record (status, generation, target, session, provider_resource, observed contents) driven by the daemon.
models.collision: The UI says "Computer" and "Machine"; the CLI says `environment computer`; the target calls it a session.

models.is: A durable record on a `compute serve` target: a workspace or container, commands run as durable jobs. A computer IS a persistent, referenced target session.
models.collision: Stored in the target's session store, not FeltDB. `compute session create` makes one directly (no environment, no daemon).

models.is: A WorkSession record in control state: an operator entering an environment (attached) or owning a temporary one (ephemeral).
models.collision: `compute session open/close/opened` beside `compute session create/.../destroy`, which are target sessions.

models.is: A pool member that hosts computers: a `compute serve` node offering sessions. Listed by GET /targets.
models.collision: Pool members are also called providers.

models.is: A pool member answering the capability API: local (in-process engine) or remote (compute.remote@1). Session providers (workspace, container) are the substrates inside a target.
models.collision: "Provider" names three things: pool members, session substrates, and DNS providers.

models.is: A workload language runtime (wasm, node, python, …, native, shell) resolved from a pinned catalog; used by `compute run` and daemon workloads.
models.collision: Not the computer substrate: computers run whatever the target host has on PATH.

models.is: Two different things: (a) a computer project — a ProjectSpec in contents: a repository plus build/test/commands/checks; (b) a bundle project — registered revisions of workload bundles, released to node environments.
models.collision: Same word, same API prefix (/environments/{e}/projects), dispatched by whether the environment has a computer.

models.is: Three things: (a) a process of kind application in a computer; (b) an `compute init/deploy` application with versions on a provider node; (c) a project in the reserved `applications` environment.
Three things: (a) a process of kind service in a computer; (b) a bundle workload of kind service; (c) a registered shared service (`compute service register`).
A durable job in a provider's job store (filesystem on the target), with a result and a receipt. Computer operations reference jobs by id; FeltDB stores the references and events, not the jobs.
models.collision: Daemon node executions are Execution records in control state; target jobs are not.

models.is: Version: a published commit + package digest + assembly + step evidence. Rollout: a version made real in an environment (deploy/promote/rollback) with steps.
models.collision: Parallel to bundle Revisions/Deployments and to application versions.

security.finding: `compute serve` has no authentication (AllowAllAuthorizer). Anyone who reaches a target lists every session and runs commands in any computer.
The daemon presents no credential to its targets by default (pool token_env unset, including the launcher), so every computer is owned by "anonymous" on its target.
Workspace computers are directories under one OS user on one host: no filesystem, process, or network isolation between computers or from the target.
A loopback daemon without TLS admits requests with no credential (development mode). The launcher runs this way.
Configuration values are passed as environment variables into every process and job in the computer; there is no secret type distinct from configuration.
Any operator with read scope can read any computer view (desired contents, configuration keys, endpoints); only mutations are owner-bound.

gaps.current: Targets accept any caller (AllowAllAuthorizer); the daemon authenticates to targets with nothing.
gaps.desired: Targets trust only their control plane (a credential or mTLS), and sessions belong to the daemon's identity.
gaps.impact: Anyone who reaches a target controls every computer on it; the daemon is not actually the authority.
gaps.next: Give `compute serve` a required credential and the pool a token for it; the launcher generates both.

gaps.current: Three deployment models: applications, bundle projects (node environments), computer versions/rollouts.
gaps.desired: One: versions reconciled into an environment's computer.
gaps.impact: Three vocabularies, three code paths, and work that still runs on the daemon host.
gaps.next: Decide the fate of node environments and applications: port their features (zero-downtime switch, ingress, domains) to computers, then retire or wrap them.

gaps.current: Default control state is a local file; FeltDB is opt-in.
gaps.desired: FeltDB as the one authority, or the file backend stated as a development convenience everywhere.
gaps.impact: Contradicts the durability contract; the launcher never uses FeltDB.
gaps.next: Decide and document; make `compute` use FeltDB when configured and say which it uses in the UI.

gaps.current: Machine loss and target unreachability are not detected for computers without processes; the view keeps "running".
gaps.desired: Every computer is periodically confirmed with its target; unreachable/lost is visible and actionable.
gaps.impact: The UI shows healthy computers that do not exist.
gaps.next: Add a session liveness check to the controller's running step independent of processes; surface "unreachable".

gaps.current: Computers are workspaces (native processes) or unverified containers.
gaps.desired: Containers verified; microVMs (Firecracker/KVM); WASM sandboxes; GPU.
gaps.impact: No isolation for computers; features advertised but not provided.
gaps.next: Verify the container provider against a real engine in CI; then a Firecracker session provider.

gaps.current: Target features describe the host (`containers` = docker on PATH), not the computer.
gaps.desired: Features describe what a computer on the target can be, verified live.
gaps.impact: Placement puts a "containers" computer in a workspace.
gaps.next: Split host features from substrate; check engine liveness.

gaps.current: No Fly/Railway/Render/cloud/bare-metal provisioning; targets must already run `compute serve`.
gaps.desired: Provider adapters that materialize targets or computers.
gaps.impact: "Put software on Railway" is impossible.
gaps.next: Define a provisioning interface (materialize a target) and one adapter.

gaps.current: Targets are configured in a pool file; network, GPU model, nested virtualization are not discovered.
gaps.desired: Discovery of machines and their capabilities.
gaps.impact: Placement only knows what a file says.
gaps.next: Liveness-checked feature discovery; optional registration of targets with the control plane.

gaps.current: persistent_storage, public_endpoint, terminal are requestable (UI checkboxes) but offered by no provider.
gaps.desired: Either implemented or not offered.
gaps.impact: Dead-end options.
gaps.next: Hide unavailable options using GET /targets; implement persistent volumes and public endpoints.

gaps.current: Bundle workloads and applications execute on the daemon host.
gaps.desired: The daemon coordinates; computers execute.
gaps.impact: The daemon is both coordinator and executor.
gaps.next: Covered by G-ARCH-2.

gaps.current: No cancellation or timeout controls in the UI; jobs have timeouts in the API.
gaps.desired: Cancel/retry for every job from every surface.
gaps.impact: Stuck builds need the CLI or waiting.
gaps.evidence: api: POST /compute/jobs/{job}/cancel has no computer-level route
gaps.next: Add cancel for computer jobs and operations.

gaps.current: Local folders must be Git repositories; no upload.
gaps.desired: Any folder.
gaps.impact: Non-Git projects cannot run.
gaps.next: Upload a folder as an artifact into the computer.

gaps.current: Endpoints are target-host:port; no domains, TLS, or ingress for computer applications.
gaps.desired: Public endpoints with domains and certificates.
gaps.impact: Production traffic cannot reach computer applications properly.
gaps.next: Route domains to computer endpoints through the existing network layer.

gaps.current: Database/Redis are command templates that assume binaries on the host.
gaps.desired: Managed service images/volumes.
gaps.impact: Templates fail where binaries are absent.
gaps.next: Depends on container computers and volumes.

gaps.current: A release restarts processes (downtime); bundle releases have zero-downtime switching.
gaps.desired: Zero-downtime rollouts for computers.
gaps.impact: Production updates interrupt traffic.
gaps.next: Two instances behind a switched endpoint inside the computer.

gaps.current: A version is a commit and a digest; no artifact is kept.
gaps.desired: Stored, verifiable artifacts (build outputs) per version.
gaps.impact: A version cannot be redeployed if the repository changes history.
gaps.next: Store the package (and optional build outputs) in the artifact store.

gaps.current: No approvals, no protected environments, no deploy freezes.
gaps.desired: Promotion policy per environment.
gaps.impact: Anyone with deploy scope who owns both environments promotes.
gaps.next: Environment policy for promotion (approvals, required checks).

gaps.current: Targets, credentials, audit, node upgrades, runtimes, placement explanation are CLI-only.
gaps.desired: Every capability visible.
gaps.impact: Operators need the terminal for setup and diagnosis.
gaps.next: Add Manage pages for targets and access.

gaps.current: The browser certification package fails; browser tests do not run in CI.
gaps.desired: Browser tests in CI.
gaps.impact: UI regressions ship (one already did).
gaps.next: Install Chromium in CI; fix the certification for the new home route.

gaps.current: 52 commands have broken or missing help; `compute session` mixes target sessions and work sessions.

gaps.impact: Discoverability.

gaps.current: No versioning of the Compute API; routes without any client (/info, /metrics, …).

gaps.current: Agents are operators; no delegation, budgets, or per-agent audit identity.

gaps.impact: An agent with deploy scope can do everything a human can.
gaps.next: Scoped, expiring agent credentials tied to an owner.
